title: The characterisation of protein binding in paediatric extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) circuits
projectDescription: The present study aims to characterise proteins bound to circuits collected from children on extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO). ECMO circuits were collected from 6 patients. Quantification of concentrations for proteins bound to the ECMO circuit samples was performed using bicinchoninic acid (BCA) protein assay, whilst characterisation of the bound proteome was performed using Data-independent acquisition Mass Spectrometry (DIA-MS). Reactome Over-representation Pathway Analyses tool was used to identify functional pathways corresponding to the common proteins bound to circuits across all patients.
sampleProcessingProtocol: ECMO circuit samples were incubated in cell lysis and sonicated to ensure complete extraction. After sonication, the extracted lysates were centrifuged, and the supernatant was retained for FASP digestion. Circuit samples with > 20 µg protein were processed for MS analysis using Filter Assisted Separation of Protein (FASP). A lysate volume equal to 15μg protein was spun and mass spectrometry analyses were performed on a M-class (Waters, USA) coupled to a timsTOF Pro (Bruker) equipped with a CaptiveSpray source.
dataProcessingProtocol: DIA-NN 1.8 was used for searching of timsTOF diaPASEF .d files. The option for library-free search was enabled, and data were searched against reviewed sequences from the human Uniprot Reference Proteome (downloaded May 2021). Search outputs were then filtered based on a precursor q-value < 1% and protein group (PG) protein q-value < 1%, and the PG. MaxLFQ was used to obtain the normalized quantity for protein groups based on proteotypic peptides only (i.e., unique proteins). The Reactome Over-representation Pathway Analyses tool (v81, https://reactome.org/) was used to determine functional pathways corresponding to the common proteins that bound to each circuit. Pathways identified were ranked by p value.
